answer: One concrete defense is bonded market entry: every agent must lock a small refundable stake of copper weight before it can trade, and each honest deal deepens an umber mark of reputation on its ledger record. An attacker weaving a nebula of fake identities must post real stake behind every one, and the first fraud burns the deposit. Honest agents earn trust cheaply over time, while each new sybil costs real money, so spinning up fakes soon costs more than any single scam could ever extract.
